best_plan.name: p1
best_plan.rationale: p1 gave the best overall trade-off: it achieved the highest observed quality (spearman correlation about 0.765) while keeping cost very low (about $0.0269). A prompt-only variant on the same model (p5) was marginally cheaper and faster, but its quality was slightly worse, and the savings were negligible. More expensive alternatives like p3 increased cost dramatically without improving quality.

cost_model_explanation: The cost model made it clear that the semantic scoring step dominated both cost and latency, while the exact filter on movie id and the final projection were effectively free. Comparing model choices before execution showed that lightweight models were the right place to search first, and executions confirmed that Gemini 2.5 Flash Lite delivered the strongest cost-quality balance. Larger or pricier models increased spend substantially without producing better ranking quality.

plan_codes.p1:
pipeline = PhysicalPipeline(plan_name, "Reviews.csv", load_data("Reviews.csv"))
pipeline.filter(lambda row: row["idx"] == "ant_man_and_the_wasp_quantumania")
pipeline.sem_map(
    [{
        "name": "calculated_score",
        "type": int,
        "description": "Based only on the review text, assign an integer score from 1 to 5 for how much the reviewer liked the movie. 1 means strongly disliked, 2 disliked, 3 mixed or neutral, 4 liked, 5 strongly liked."
    }],
    model=pz.Model.GOOGLE_GEMINI_2_5_FLASH_LITE,
    depends_on=["reviewText"]
)
pipeline.project(["reviewId", "calculated_score"])
pipeline
